newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: WORLD BANK RELEASES ZAMBIA $70 MLN BOP SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK RELEASES ZAMBIA $70 MLN BOP SUPPORT.

text.p: The World Bank has released $70 million to Zambia for balance of payment support under the Economic Recovery and Investment Promotion Credit (ERIP), finance minister Ronald Penza said on Friday.
"The International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank has released a sum of $70 million for balance of payment support. This represents the second tranche of ERIP," Penza said.

"The release of the second tranche of ERIP follows the successful Consultative Group meeting held in Paris last July and Zambia's having met the specific conditionalities attaching to the credit," he added.
The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) maintained normal aid flows to Zambia despite an aid squeeze effected by western governments in mid-1996 over governance concerns.

Western governments led by the United States froze balance of payment support to this impoverished southern African country after the government changed electoral laws to ban some candidates, including former president Kenneth Kaunda, from contesting presidential elections.
Seven parties boycotted elections, which president Frederick Chiluba's Movememt for Multiparty Democracy won by a landslide.
The bilateral donors only lifted the aid squeeze in July 1997.
Kaunda on Thursday urged donors to maintain the aid squeeze on the country to force the Chiluba government to effect democratic reform.
The opposition is demanding that last year's controversial elections be nullified and that a fresh poll be run this year.
